1315: Monks teach us to radiate loving-kindness to all beings — friend or stranger, all the same.
Monks teach us to radiate loving-kindness to ourselves first — before others, they say.
Monks teach us to show compassion to all beings — small or large, all the same.
1316: Having loving-kindness and compassion for others is what makes a community hold together.
Having loving-kindness and compassion for oneself matters just as much.
Having loving-kindness and compassion for animals is part of the same teaching.
1317: A hot-tempered person, if they often cultivate mindfulness, can learn to pause before speaking.
A hot-tempered person, if they often chant in the evening, can become much calmer.
A hot-tempered person, if they never practise at all, will stay exactly as they are.
1318: When merit-making is done, Thais often say sadhu three times over.
When merit-making is done, Thais often pour water and dedicate the merit.
When merit-making is done, Thais often kneel and bow three times.
1319: Elders like to teach 'just accept it, nothing is certain' when we lose someone.
Elders like to teach 'do good, receive good' when we're tempted to cut corners.
Elders like to teach 'be patient, it will pass' when we want to give up.
1320: He says that since he turned to the temple and started practising, he sleeps far better.
He says that since he stopped drinking and started practising, his life has changed a lot.
He says that since his father died and he started practising, his life has changed a lot.
1321: The old folk believe that if the mind has mindfulness and keeps the precepts, no harm can come to it.
The old folk believe that if the house has a spirit house, ghosts won't dare come and disturb it.
The old folk believe that if a child is given a bad name, misfortune will follow it about.
1322: Thais believe the devas watch over those who make merit at the temple.
Thais believe the devas watch over travellers on a long journey.
Thais believe the devas reward those who do good and keep the precepts.
1323: When pouring the water libation, Thais often dedicate merit to their parents first.
When pouring the water libation, Thais often say the words under their breath.
When pouring the water libation, Thais usually pour it onto the earth outside.
1324: The Buddha's teachings are collected in the Tipitaka, which runs to many volumes.
The Buddha's teachings are collected in the Tipitaka, written down some centuries after him.
The Buddha's teachings are remembered in the Dhammapada, the best known of the collections.
1325: Many wonder what kind of merit-making suits a busy person.
Many wonder what kind of merit-making the Buddha himself recommended.
Many wonder what kind of offering a monk may actually accept.
1326: Luang Por Chah taught: 'If it isn't good, let it go. If it won't go, leave it be.'
Luang Por Chah taught: 'If you are angry, watch it. If you watch it, it goes.'
Luang Por Chah taught: 'Let go a little, get a little peace. Let go a lot, get a lot.'
1327: Luang Por Chah once said: 'Nibbana lies at the end of craving.'
Luang Por Chah once said: 'The practice is the same wherever you sit.'
Luang Por Chah once wrote: 'Nibbana lies on the shores of death.'

1317.nat: A hot-tempered person, if they often cultivate mindfulness, can become much calmer.
